sections.title: Whose is it? The owner plus -é
sections.content: You know *kié* ("whose") and the words *enyém*, *tiéd* and *övé* ("mine", "yours", "his/hers"). For an owner who is a name or a noun, add *-é* to the owner and drop the thing owned: *Kié ez a táska? – Péteré.* ("Whose is this bag? – Péter's.") The *-é* stands for "the one belonging to", so there is no noun after it.

sections.title: The rules
sections.content: The ending is always *-é*; vowel harmony does not matter, so you never meet *-a* or *-e* variants. A final *-a/-e* lengthens first, just as before other endings: *Anna* becomes *Annáé*, *anya* becomes *anyáé*. With a plural owner the *-k* of the plural stays and *-é* follows: *a szomszédok* gives *a szomszédoké*.

items.spanish: Kié ez a ház? – A szomszédoké.
items.english: Whose is this house? – The neighbours'.

items.spanish: A bőrönd nem az enyém, hanem Annáé.
items.english: The suitcase isn't mine, it's Anna's.

sections.content: *az enyém, a tiéd, az övé* cover "I, you, he/she"; *-é* does the same job for any other owner: a name, *anya*, *a szomszéd*. In the answer you can put *a/az* before it (*Az anyáé*) or leave it off (*Péteré*).
